subject: Post-call: eval synthesis, recommended models & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@finisys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: eval synthesis, recommended models & next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and my recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Recap (what you shared)
- Primary use: real-time customer support assistant (multi-turn), 2–3 concise responses per interaction.
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for 512-token completions; p50 goal < 40ms.
- Throughput target: sustained ~180–220 requests/sec (sustained), spikes to ~350 rps during peak.
- Context window: baseline 512 tokens, plan to evaluate 2–4k contexts for advanced cases.
- Quality: highest priority is extraction accuracy and concise, non-hallucinated answers.

Redwood-recommended models (first-pass)
1) redwood-13b-8bit (recommended baseline) — good balance of quality / latency.  Expect verified profile: ~180 TPS sustained on our medium-sized dedicated pool; latency p50 ~38ms, p90 ~95ms, p99 ~180ms (512-token).
2) redwood-7b-q4f16 (cost-optimized) — ~300 TPS, p50 ~25ms, p90 ~65ms; slightly lower factuality on rare edge prompts.
3) redwood-13b-4k (long-context variant) — for 2–4k evaluation; p50/p90/p99 increase as context grows (links below).

Notes on quantization & quality
- Quantized runs (q4f16/q8) will reduce cost and improve TPS but can introduce subtle token-level regressions; recommend running your curated prompt set vs production traces for regression detection.
- We will surface example failure modes in the eval report (hallucination frequency, truncation on long context, instruction-following regressions).

Artifacts I attached / links
- redwood_perf_profiles_20270607.pdf (short Redwood-verified perf profiles for recommended models) [attachment stub]
- finisys_prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts you can approve, includes edge-cases) [attachment stub]
- redwood_benchmarks_20270607.csv (internal run summaries) [attachment stub]
- Shared dashboards: https://app.redwood.com/benchmarks/DEAL-2027-0347

Proposed next steps
- Permission to run a short baseline benchmarking job using the provided prompt set (2–4 hours). We recommend using a dedicated medium pool to reproduce production-ish contention.
- You send a small production trace extract or confirm we can use the attached prompt set.
- Schedule a 30-min joint review of the benchmark results (I can do Thurs/Fri this week).

If this aligns, I’ll ask Solutions to queue the run and share the Redwood-verified profile snapshot + a short eval report (latency percentiles, TPS, token cost, and a short quality regression section).

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we green-light a run: 

1) The latency numbers you listed — are those measured at our target concurrency (180–220 rps) or single-client? We need end-to-end p95 that includes network and prefix caching overheads.
2) For the 2–4k context case: roughly how much does p95 degrade vs the 512 baseline on redwood-13b-8bit? We have long-reference answers for some claims and need those preserved.
3) Quantization risk: our legal/compliance team will want to know if q4f16 materially increases hallucination rate (we have low tolerance). Can you include any regression numbers from similar customers?

Also, can you confirm whether the benchmarking job would touch any PII if we share a small anonymized sample of transcripts? We want to confirm data handling.

Olivia
Director, AI Product
Finisys
olivia@finisys.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: eval synthesis, recommended models & next steps

Hi Olivia — quick answers and concrete numbers from our Redwood-verified profiles + guidance on regressions. See inline below.

1) Latency context: our published profiles reflect end-to-end inference time inside Redwood’s serving layer (network-to-inference). For your concurrency band (180–220 rps) we replicate this by running sustained multi-client load with representative prefix caching enabled. The p95 figures I quoted include both batching and typical network overheads observed in our hosted/Dedicated runs.

2) 2–4k context impact (redwood-13b-8bit): based on recent runs with customer-like prompts, expect ~1.6–2.1x increase in p95 vs 512-token baselines. Example verified snapshot (attached):
- 512 tokens: p50 38ms / p90 95ms / p99 180ms (sustained ~180 TPS)
- 2k tokens: p50 95ms / p90 210ms / p99 420ms (sustained ~80–120 TPS)
- 4k tokens: p50 210ms / p90 420ms / p99 900ms (sustained ~40–60 TPS)

3) Quantization & quality regressions: we track a small set of regression metrics on instruction-following and fact-extraction tasks. Typical q4f16 runs on redwood-13b show: 
- small increase in token-level edit distance on extraction tasks (~2–4% absolute)
- a ~1–2% increase in hallucination flags on our internal checklist for long-context prompts (these are context-sensitive; not universal)
- we annotate example failures in the eval report and recommend prompt-level mitigations (clarity templates, verification hooks).

Data handling: benchmarking jobs can be run in a staging VPC; we will not persist raw PII outside the job unless you instruct us. If you send an anonymized transcript sample we will work under your data handling controls and can execute under a standard NDA or SOC2 controls as required.

Suggested concrete plan
- Approve the attached prompt set or provide a sanitized trace (1k–5k rows).
- We’ll run two passes: (A) baseline on redwood-13b-8bit and (B) cost-optimized on redwood-7b-q4f16. Each pass includes perf (TPS, p50/p90/p99), token-cost estimate, and a short quality regression appendix with labeled examples.
- Deliverable: single PDF report + CSV of per-prompt outputs + dashboard link within 48 hours of run completion.

Proposed times: Wed 9–11am or Thu 2–4pm PT to kick off. I can also coordinate Solutions/Infra if you want a dedicated pool for more realistic contention.

If this works I’ll queue the run and share the final Redwood-verified profile snapshot + the short report.

—
Marissa Cole
